text: RN1 Transcriptómica y dinámica de linajes. Lineage hierarchy trees + transition-probability matrices (.json); average expression per cell type (.csv/.tsv: rows=key genes pax2a/foxc1a/tfap2a, cols=hpf or clusters); curated lineage-restriction notes from lineage-tracing literature (.md/.txt). File types: .json, .csv, .tsv, .md, .txt.

RN2 Estructura proteica y complejos. 3D coords of experimentally resolved structures (RA receptors; TFs tfap2a/foxc1a/pax2a/wt1a; Notch/Jagged2a extracellular domains; collagen-fibronectin complexes; tubular claudins); AlphaFold metadata (.json) for proteins without a zebrafish crystal structure; predicted-aligned-error (.pae/.npy) for complexes (Jagged2a-Notch, Foxc1a-Pitx2); small molecules/drugs for perturbation docking (.mol2/.sdf: RA, DEAB). File types: .pdb, .cif, .mmcif, .json, .pae, .npy, .mol2, .sdf.

RN3 Redes de señalización y parámetros cinéticos. Signaling/state-transition trees + simulation env variables (.json); average expression + biophysical constants (.csv/.tsv); lineage-restriction summaries (.md/.txt); systems-biology descriptions / curated object skeletons (.xml/.cellml/.sed-ml); BioNetGen rule-based models (.bngl) packaged by the substrate → equations → Morpheus .xml. File types: .json, .csv, .tsv, .md, .txt, .xml, .cellml, .sed-ml, .bngl.

text: RN4 Microambiente bioquímico. Mass-spec metabolomics/lipidomics (.mzML/.mzXML; MCP wrapper → .csv); spatial lipid distribution maps (.imML); 2D/3D O2/pH gradient maps for Morpheus (.json/.yaml); kinetic time-series (ion fluxes, intracellular Ca during tubulogenesis) (.csv/.tsv); local metabolic pathway maps (.xml KEGG/MetaCyc). File types: .mzML, .mzXML, .imML, .json, .yaml, .csv, .tsv, .xml.

RN5 Bioeléctrica. Spatial coords + absolute membrane potential (.csv); high-density temporal matrices from fluorescence/voltage sensors (.mat); molecular config (ion channels, surface densities, permeability, activation states) (.json); voltage-imaging video with segmentation masks (.ome/.tiff). File types: .csv, .mat, .json, .ome, .tiff.

RN6 Biomecánica pasiva y ECM. Affinity matrices, basal cortical tension, cell-friction coefficients for Morpheus (.json); regional stiffness profiles (Young's kPa from AFM) (.csv); SHG / super-res IF of collagen-fibronectin (.ome/.tiff); static scaffold/basal-membrane geometry templates (.xml); FEA meshes of static deformation / viscoelastic stress as boundary conditions (.vtk/.vtu). File types: .json, .csv, .ome, .tiff, .xml, .vtk, .vtu.

RN7 Mecánica activa y dinámica de fluidos. Cell/segment/node-indexed flow vectors, velocity, pressure (.csv/.tsv); high-density 3D meshes with velocity gradients + stress tensors (.vtu/.vtp); velocimetry/AFM matrices, elastic constants, traction fields (.mat); fluid-env physical properties (.json); CFD mesh/solution interchange (.cgns). File types: .csv, .tsv, .vtu, .vtp, .mat, .json, .cgns.

DanioCODE. Identify which regulatory elements respond to which signals and when. Data: Functional genome (open-source) of zebrafish. Feeds RN1, RN3.
Reactome. Metabolic pathway analysis, gene interaction and signaling (zebrafish via computational orthology inference). Data: Pathways, gene interaction, cross-species stimulation. Feeds RN3, RN4.
GEO NCBI. Gene-expression analysis and interactions. Data: Gene count/expression data from published papers. Feeds RN1, RN8, RN9.
UCSC Cell Browser. Visualize lineage trajectories and cell populations; aggregates published scRNA-seq datasets. Data: Cell lineages across body regions / species. Feeds RN1, RN8.
STRING DB. Which proteins work with which genes and which signaling is activated (PREDICTIVE). Data: Protein interaction data (predicted). Feeds RN2, RN3.
IntAct. Complement to BioGRID and STRING — PHYSICAL, verified interactions. Data: Molecular interactions from published papers. Feeds RN2, RN3.

BioGRID. How genes interact with each other and with proteins; GENETIC interactions (what happens to the embryo if you alter two genes at once). Data: Gene-gene / gene-protein interaction repository. Feeds RN3, RN12.

Ensembl Zebrafish (Danio rerio). Functional human equivalents (a dictionary); the authoritative identifier resolver behind the DATA INAMOVIBLE. Data: Promoter sequences, gene annotation/comparison, variants, human orthologs. Feeds RN1, RN2, RN11.

Zebrafish pronephros tubulogenesis and epithelial identity maintenance are reliant on the polarity proteins Prkc iota and zeta..  niche RN1 domain N3 entities pax2a podxl wt1a wt1b stage None tissue None

The zebrafish pronephros provides an excellent in vivo system to study the mechanisms of vertebrate nephron development. When and how renal progenitors in the zebrafish embryo undergo tubulogenesis to form nephrons is poorly understood, but is known to involve a mesenchymal to epithelial transition (MET) and the acquisition of polarity. Here, we determined the precise timing of these events in pronephros tubulogenesis. As the ternary polarity complex is an essential regulator of epithelial cell polarity across tissues, we performed gene knockdown studies to assess the roles of the related factors atypical protein kinase C iota and zeta (prkcι, prkcζ). We found that prkcι and prkcζ serve partially redundant functions to establish pronephros tubule epithelium polarity. Further, the loss of prkcι or the combined knockdown of prkcι/ζ disrupted proximal tubule morphogenesis and podocyte migration due to cardiac defects that prevented normal fluid flow to the kidney. Surprisingly, tubule cells in prkcι/ζ morphants displayed ectopic expression of the transcription factor pax2a and the podocyte-associated genes wt1a, wt1b, and podxl, suggesting that prkcι/ζ are needed to maintain renal epithelial identity. Knockdown of genes essential for cardiac contractility and vascular flow to the kidney, such as tnnt2a, or elimination of pronephros fluid output through knockdown of the intraflagellar transport gene ift88, was not associated with ectopic pronephros gene expression, thus suggesting a unique role for prkcι/ζ in maintaining tubule epithelial identity separate from the consequence of disruptions to renal fluid flow. Interestingly, knockdown of pax2a, but not wt1a, was sufficient to rescue ectopic tubule gene expression in prkcι/ζ morphants.
